newsitem.title: IRAN: Pakistan asks for Iranian help on Afghanistan-Iran.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan asks for Iranian help on Afghanistan-Iran.

text.p: Pakistan told Iran on Monday it was ready to accept a joint plan to find an end to the war in neighbouring Afghanistan, Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said.

Velayati, quoted by Tehran radio, said a Pakistani delegation informed him of Islamabad's position at talks in Tehran, where the media has accused Pakistan of supporting the radical Taleban which seized Kabul last month.
"The Pakistani government declared that it wanted an end to the Afghan war and reiterated that Pakistan did not want a particular group to rule in Afghanistan," Velayati said.
He was speaking after holding talks with a Pakistani delegation lead by an envoy of Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, which arrived in Tehran earlier in the day.
"Those who thought that the Taleban group could have absolute power on the Afghan scene have realised their errors, because a government that relies on foreigners will not last long," Velayati said.
Shi'ite Moslem Iran recognises the government of Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani, driven out of the capital Kabul by the Sunni Taleban militia in September.
Iran's media has accused Pakistan of setting up the Taleban with backing from the United States and funding from Saudi Arabia to counter Iran's influence in the region.
Iran has condemned what it calls foreign meddling in Afghanistan and called on warring factions to seek a power-sharing agreement.
The Taleban and their opponents said on Monday they were ready to accept a Pakistani-brokered ceasefire, but both sides set conditions to any accord and were still locked in battle.
